sketchMechanisms: Optional chaining — accessing a property through a chain of optionals silently returns nil if any link is absent, collapsing the entire expression to nothing.
Unification failure — Prolog tries to make two terms equal and simply fails when they cannot unify, producing no solution.
A value is moved into a closure that is called once (FnOnce), after which the original binding is consumed and can never be used again.
